pages.headline: PSLV-C62 fails in third stage
pages.what: ISRO's PSLV-C62, the 64th PSLV mission, failed after an anomaly in the solid third stage, causing loss of the EOS-N1 (Anvesha) satellite and 15 co-passengers. It was also the 9th dedicated commercial mission of NSIL.
key: 64th PSLV flight; 9th dedicated NSIL commercial mission
Payload: EOS-N1 (Anvesha) plus 15 co-passenger satellites
Failure in solid third stage near burnout
Second PSLV failure in a row after PSLV-C61 (May 2025, EOS-09)
PSLV stages: solid, liquid (Vikas), solid, liquid
pages.static: PSLV stages; NSIL as ISRO's commercial arm.
pages.angle: Calling the second stage solid.

pages.headline: Gaganyaan plan for 2027
pages.what: ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan said the Gaganyaan programme is planned for 2027, with three uncrewed missions to precede the crewed flight. The crew of the human spaceflight programme are called Gaganyatri.
key: Crewed flight planned for 2027
Three uncrewed missions first
Crew name: Gaganyatri
Statement made 30 January 2026
pages.angle: Miscounting the number of precursor missions.

pages.headline: Pixxel-led EO constellation with IN-SPACe
pages.what: A Pixxel-led consortium signed an agreement with IN-SPACe to design, build and operate India's first national Earth Observation constellation under a PPP model. It marks a shift from government-built to industry-operated infrastructure.
key: Consortium: Pixxel, Piersight Space, Satsure Analytics India, Dhruva Space
12 satellites: optical, multispectral, SAR, hyperspectral
Rs 1,200 crore over five years
PPP model
IN-SPACe is the authorising agency; NSIL is ISRO's commercial arm
pages.static: Space sector reforms (2020); IN-SPACe and NSIL.
pages.angle: Confusing IN-SPACe with NSIL.

pages.headline: Long-duration scramjet test
pages.what: DRDO completed a long-duration ground test of a full-scale, actively cooled scramjet combustor at DRDL, Hyderabad, running over 12 minutes of sustained supersonic combustion for the Hypersonic Cruise Missile programme.
key: Test at DRDL, Hyderabad; over 12 minutes
Actively cooled, full-scale combustor
Scramjet: air-breathing, above Mach 5, supersonic combustion
No rotating compressor; needs assisted take-off
Typically uses hydrogen fuel and atmospheric oxygen
pages.angle: Assuming scramjets work from standstill.
pages.remember: Scramjet: fast to start, none from zero.

pages.headline: Reusable rocket technology
pages.what: Reusable launch technology has cut launch costs by 5 to 20 times by recovering the expensive first stage. India's expendable PSLV and LVM-3 discard their stages, while ISRO is working on a winged RLV and stage-recovery systems.
key: First stage holds engines, avionics and tanks: recovered
Over 90% of liftoff mass is propellant; payload under 4%
Falcon 9 uses retro-propulsion to land
PSLV and LVM-3 are expendable
India: winged RLV and stage-recovery systems
pages.angle: Mistaking propellant for payload in the mass breakdown.

pages.headline: ISRO's NGLV and the missing space law
pages.what: Analysis of ISRO highlighted the Next-Generation Launch Vehicle, a partly reusable design for up to 30 tonnes to LEO, and the lack of a comprehensive space law. IN-SPACe has launched a technology adoption fund.
key: NGLV: up to 30 tonnes to LEO, partially reusable
IN-SPACe technology adoption fund for prototypes
No comprehensive national space law
ISRO acts as fallback regulator without statutory authority
Reforms need legal roles for IN-SPACe and NSIL
pages.static: Space Activities Bill debate; liberalisation since 2020.
pages.angle: Assuming a national space law exists.
pages.remember: No space law yet; NGLV is 30 tonnes.

pages.headline: Fast-spinning asteroid 2025 MN45
pages.what: Asteroid 2025 MN45, found in the first images of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile, is the fastest-spinning asteroid over 500 m in diameter, rotating once every 1.88 minutes.
key: Rotation: once every 1.88 minutes
Diameter about 710 m; main belt between Mars and Jupiter
Discovered in Rubin's first images (released 23 June 2025)
Rubin: 8.4 m Simonyi Survey Telescope, 3,200-megapixel camera
pages.angle: Confusing minutes with hours.

pages.headline: ARIES studies a contact binary
pages.what: Astronomers at ARIES used the Devasthal Fast Optical Telescope and NASA's TESS to study a low-mass W Ursae Majoris contact binary star and found strong magnetic activity and star spots.
key: Institute: ARIES, under Department of Science and Technology
Instruments: Devasthal Fast Optical Telescope, NASA's TESS
W UMa: eclipsing contact binary sharing outer atmosphere
Orbital periods about 0.25 to 1 day
Findings: strong magnetic activity, star spots
pages.angle: Confusing contact binaries with compact-object pairs.
pages.remember: W UMa: two stars in one shared envelope.

pages.headline: Webb maps dark matter
pages.what: Astronomers used observations from the James Webb Space Telescope to unveil a detailed map of dark matter, a hypothesised invisible form of matter inferred from its gravitational effects.
key: Dark matter does not emit, absorb or reflect light
Inferred from gravitational effects
Universe: normal matter 5%, dark matter 27%, dark energy 68%
Map based on James Webb Space Telescope data
pages.angle: Swapping the dark matter and dark energy shares.

pages.headline: Mpemba effect simulated
pages.what: Researchers at JNCASR created the first simulation of ice formation that reproduces the Mpemba effect, in which hot water can freeze faster than cold water.
key: JNCASR: autonomous body under DST
First simulation reproducing the Mpemba effect
Named after Tanzanian student Erasto Mpemba (1969)
Aristotle described it in Meteorologica
Water passes through short-lived intermediate molecular states
pages.angle: Placing JNCASR under the wrong department.
pages.remember: Hot freezes first: Mpemba, via DST's JNCASR.

pages.headline: Ocean heat content hits a record in 2025
pages.what: A study found oceans absorbed an extra 23 zettajoules of heat in 2025, the most recorded. Sea surface temperatures were about 0.5 degrees C above the 1981-2010 average.
key: Extra heat absorbed: 23 zettajoules, highest since 1960s
Oceans absorb about 90% of excess greenhouse heat
Sea surface temperature about 0.5 C above 1981-2010 average
Warming raises stratification, cuts oxygen and nutrient mixing
Effects: marine heat waves, coral bleaching, stronger cyclones
pages.static: Ocean stratification; marine heat waves; phytoplankton and the food chain.
pages.angle: Believing warming increases ocean mixing.

pages.headline: Red aurora at Hanle
pages.what: A rare blood-red auroral display was captured by the all-sky camera at the Indian Astronomical Observatory, Hanle, in the Hanle Dark Sky Reserve in Ladakh.
key: All-sky camera at Indian Astronomical Observatory, Hanle
About 4,500 m, Changthang region, Ladakh
India's first Dark Sky Reserve (Dec 2022)
Notified by the Ladakh administration
Managed by Indian Institute of Astrophysics (DST)
pages.angle: Naming ISRO as the manager.
pages.remember: Hanle sky is managed by IIA.

pages.headline: Gujarat's BSL-4 laboratory
pages.what: Union Home Minister Amit Shah laid the foundation stone in Gandhinagar for India's first State-funded BSL-4 laboratory, to be run by the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre under the Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission.
key: First State-funded BSL-4 lab in India
Run by Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre
Second civilian BSL-4 after NIV Pune
DRDO's defence BSL-4 lab is at Gwalior
Pathogens: Ebola, Nipah, Marburg, CCHF, Kyasanur Forest Disease
pages.angle: Calling it the first civilian BSL-4 lab.
pages.remember: BSL-4: Gandhinagar second civilian, Pune first.

pages.headline: FDA approves Zycubo for Menkes disease
pages.what: The US FDA approved Zycubo (copper histidinate) as the first treatment for Menkes disease in paediatric patients.
key: Drug: Zycubo (copper histidinate)
First approved treatment for Menkes disease
Cause: mutation in ATP7A gene on the X chromosome
Impairs copper transport
Mostly affects male infants
pages.angle: Saying the disease mainly affects females.

pages.headline: Kamala: India's first genome-edited rice
pages.what: Scientist Satendra Mangrauthia received a Vigyan Yuva award for developing Kamala, described as India's first genome-edited rice.
key: Kamala (DRR Dhan 100): first genome-edited rice variety of India
Developed by ICAR (rice research institute, Hyderabad)
Genome editing changes native genes; SDN-1 adds no foreign DNA
Different from transgenic (GM) crops like Bt cotton
Award: Vigyan Yuva (Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar)
pages.static: SDN-1 and SDN-2 genome-edited plants exempt from GM rules (2022); GEAC regulation of GM crops.
pages.angle: Calling genome-edited rice a GM crop.

pages.headline: Nipah cases in West Bengal
pages.what: Nipah virus infection was confirmed by NIV Pune in two nurses at a private hospital in Barasat, West Bengal. All 196 traced contacts tested negative.
key: Two nurses, Barasat, North 24 Parganas
Confirmed by NIV Pune on 13 January 2026
All 196 contacts negative
No licensed vaccine or specific treatment
Reservoir: fruit bats; incubation 4-14 days; first identified 1999
pages.static: Zoonoses; National Centre for Disease Control.
pages.angle: Assuming a vaccine exists.
pages.remember: Nipah: bats carry it, no licensed vaccine.

pages.headline: Biomaterials: challenges and opportunities
pages.what: Biomaterials are derived wholly or partly from biological sources or made by biological processes. They fall into drop-in, drop-out and novel types, and help India cut import dependence on fossil-based plastics.
key: Drop-in: chemically identical to petroleum products, e.g. bio-PET
Drop-out: chemically different, e.g. polylactic acid (PLA)
Novel: new properties, e.g. self-healing materials
Bioplastics market about USD 500 million (2024)
Risks: feedstock competition with food, weak composting
pages.angle: Swapping the examples of drop-in and drop-out.
pages.remember: Bio-PET drops in; PLA drops out.

pages.headline: Marine and space biotechnology
pages.what: A feature argued that India underuses its marine bioresources. Seaweed cultivation is about 70,000 tonnes a year and key products like agar and carrageenan are imported. ISRO runs a microgravity biology programme.
key: Seaweed cultivation about 70,000 tonnes a year
Imports agar, carrageenan, alginates
Coastline over 11,000 km; EEZ about 2 million sq km
Initiatives: Deep Ocean Mission, BioE3, Blue Economy
ISRO microgravity biology programme
pages.angle: Overstating the size of the EEZ.
pages.remember: Two million sq km of sea to farm.

pages.headline: Shrutlekh AI tool
pages.what: MeitY demonstrated Shrutlekh, an AI tool under BHASHINI for real-time multilingual speech-to-text translation of speeches.
key: Tool: Shrutlekh, under BHASHINI
Real-time multilingual speech-to-text translation
BHASHINI: National Language Translation Mission
Over 22 scheduled languages
Bhashadaan crowdsourcing initiative
pages.angle: Confusing it with a document locker.

pages.headline: 6 GHz lower band de-licensed
pages.what: The Department of Telecommunications de-licensed the lower half of the 6 GHz band, 5,925-6,425 MHz, for indoor use, enabling Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7. Use on moving vehicles and oil rigs is prohibited.
key: Lower 6 GHz: 5,925-6,425 MHz
Indoor use only
Enables Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7
Prohibited on moving vehicles and oil rigs
pages.angle: Allowing outdoor mobile use.

pages.headline: Battery Pack Aadhaar draft guidelines
pages.what: The Union government released draft guidelines for a Battery Pack Aadhaar system giving each EV battery pack and industrial battery above 2 kWh a 21-character number and QR code.
key: 21-character BPAN plus QR code
EV batteries and industrial batteries above 2 kWh
Static data on BPAN: manufacturer, specifications, carbon footprint
Dynamic data on central server: health, charge cycles
Enables second-life use and recycling
pages.static: Battery waste management rules; circular economy.
pages.angle: Applying the rule to all batteries.

pages.headline: India to roll out V2V
pages.what: The Union Road Transport and Highways Minister announced that India will roll out Vehicle-to-Vehicle communication technology, which lets vehicles talk to each other directly.
key: Announced by the Road Transport and Highways Minister
Direct inter-vehicle communication
Does not rely on cellular or other third-party networks
Strengthens ADAS by sharing hidden-hazard warnings
pages.angle: Assuming it relies on cellular networks.
pages.remember: V2V: car talks to car, no tower.

pages.headline: CDS releases Military Quantum Mission framework
pages.what: The Chief of Defence Staff released a policy framework and roadmap to bring quantum technology into the armed forces. It aligns with the National Quantum Mission.
key: Aligned with National Quantum Mission, about Rs 6,000 crore, 2023-24 to 2030-31
Four pillars: communication, computing, sensing and metrology, materials and devices
QKD uses entanglement for theoretically unhackable keys
Quantum navigation can replace GPS-dependent guidance
Quantum magnetometers can detect submerged submarines
pages.static: National Quantum Mission (2023); qubits, superposition, entanglement.
pages.angle: Saying QKD depends on mathematical complexity.

pages.headline: Digital climate atlas for agriculture launched
pages.what: The Government launched ACASA-India as NICRA marked 15 years. It supports location-specific climate adaptation planning for farmers and planners.
key: ACASA-India: Atlas of Climate Adaptation in Indian Agriculture
Built by ICAR-led NARES with BISA-CIMMYT
NICRA launched by ICAR in 2011
Aim: validate and demonstrate climate-resilient technologies
Guides government investment in climate-risk mitigation
pages.static: Climate-resilient agriculture; ICAR; CIMMYT and Borlaug Institute for South Asia.
pages.angle: Confusing NICRA (ICAR) with a ministry mission.
pages.remember: NICRA 2011, ICAR; ACASA is its atlas.

pages.headline: WEF 4IR Centre for Andhra Pradesh
pages.what: The World Economic Forum announced five new Fourth Industrial Revolution Centres globally. One will be in Andhra Pradesh, the third in India after Mumbai and Telangana.
key: Five new 4IR Centres announced by the WEF
One in Andhra Pradesh
Third in India after Mumbai and Telangana
Term coined by Klaus Schwab (WEF founder), 2016
Convergence of AI, robotics, IoT, quantum computing
pages.angle: Crediting the wrong person for the term.
pages.remember: Schwab coined 4IR; Andhra is India's third centre.
